'''Set''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] character from a legend originating in<ref name="Databank" /> the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo's]]<ref name="JvS">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> [[Futhork/Legends|Futhork]] [[Writing/Legends|calligraphy]], in which he was the eternal lover of a woman named [[Veré]].<ref name="Databank" /> In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="JvS" /> these names were used as aliases by<ref name="Databank" /> [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]],<ref name="JvS" /> respectively. The pair used the archaic monikers to [[Wedding of Anakin Skywalker and Padmé Amidala/Legends|anonymously marry]], not even allowing their pastor, [[Pontifex/Legends|Pontifex]] [[Maxiron Agolerga/Legends|Maxiron Agolerga]], to know of their true identities. "Set" and "Veré" were blissfully [[Marriage/Legends|wed]], and Agolerga was [[Mind trick/Legends|instructed]] to tell no one of the ceremony, ensuring the only record of the short procession would be a scroll in his [[Brotherhood of Cognizance/Legends|Brotherhood's]] archives.<ref name="Databank" /> When Agolerga eventually learned who they really were, he informed Amidala's niece, [[Pooja Naberrie/Legends|Pooja Naberrie]], of the union.<ref name="JvS" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I remembered a story from 'Lord of the Rings' called 'The Tale of Beren and Lúthien' and transported this to the SW Galaxy. ''[&hellip;]'' What this legend is about remain''[s]'' untold. Were they happy? Did a tragedy occur? We might never know.|Tim Veekhoven|<ref name="Sompeetalay">{{Blog|teekay-421|13|They were the chosen ones}}</ref>}}
Set was created by [[Tim Veekhoven]], writing as "Sompeetalay," for the character Maxiron Agolerga's [[Databank (original)|Databank]] entry via the ''[[What's The Story?]]'' [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] feature on [[StarWars.com]].<ref name="Databank" /> The entry was written in [[February]] [[2007]] and published in early [[2008]]. The eternal lovers' motif was borrowed from a famous work of [[Wikipedia:J. R. R. Tolkien|J. R. R. Tolkien]] entitled [[Wikipedia:The Tale of Beren and Lúthien|''The Tale of Beren and Lúthien'']],<ref name="Sompeetalay" /> which details the romance between a mortal man named Beren and an Elf-maiden named Lúthien.<ref name="LOTR">{{BookCite|author=[[Wikipedia:J. R. R. Tolkien|Tolkien, J. R. R.]]|title=[[Wikipedia:The Silmarillion|The Silmarillion]]|contributor=[[Wikipedia:Christopher Tolkien|Christopher Tolkien]] (editor)|publisher=[[Wikipedia:Allen & Unwin|Allen & Unwin]]|date=1977}}</ref> Veekhoven named Set after the [[Wikipedia:Egypt|Egyptian]] [[Wikipedia:Deity|god]] [[Wikipedia:Set (mythology)|Set]].<ref name="Sompeetalay" />
